models_evaluated: three commercial DLAS software built-in models

links.effect: Three commercial DLAS vendor built-in models achieved sub-optimal performance in 20 patients.
links.quote: Three commercial DLAS vendor built-in models achieved sub-optimal performance in 20 patients.

links.effect: Custom model DSC: 0.82 prostate, 0.48 SV, 0.92 rectum; built-in: 0.73, 0.37, 0.81; significant improvement.
links.quote: This represents a significant improvement over the built-in model with DSC of 0.73, 0.37, and 0.81 for the corresponding structures.

links.effect: Failures: cystogram n=2, hip prosthesis n=2, brachytherapy seeds n=2, air in endorectal balloon n=1, non-iodinated spacer n=2, giant bladder n=1.
links.quote: The failure modes of retrained custom model were attributed to the following: cystogram (n = 2), hip prosthesis (n = 2), low dose rate brachytherapy seeds (n = 2), air in endorectal balloon(n = 1), non-iodinated spacer (n = 2), and giant bladder(n = 1).

links.effect: Manual contours: 96.5% acceptance and 3.5% consensus unacceptable; custom model: 91.3% acceptance and 8.7% consensus unacceptable.
links.quote: Compared to the acceptance rate of 96.5% and consensus unacceptable rate (i.e., both reviewers rated as unacceptable) of 3.5% achieved by manual contours, the custom model achieved a 91.3% acceptance rate and 8.7% consensus unacceptable rate.

screen.reason: Evaluates the deployment practice of using incremental local retraining on institutional data to address practice variability/performance degradation of commercial DL auto-segmentation models, comparing performance and physician acceptance rate.
